sections.h2: Where is the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office sits in the Government Center at 448 Court Place, Suite 202, in Beulah, Michigan 49617. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the phone number is 231-882-0016.

Benzie County lies in northwest lower Michigan along Lake Michigan, and its own website highlights more than 100 lakes and several square miles of state forest. Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in those townships and in the city of Frankfort is indexed at this one office.

  • The office does not prepare blank documents and its staff cannot give legal advice. It suggests an attorney or title company for drafting.
  • Recordings can be made in person, by mail, by UPS or FedEx, or through eRecording.
  • Copy requests by mail must include a self-addressed stamped envelope.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Benzie County?
sections.html:
The county page states that every document costs $30.00 to record regardless of page count. That matches the statewide figure in MCL 600.2567, which also folds the state survey fee into the $30. If one document assigns or discharges more than one instrument, add $3.00 for each extra instrument.

Benzie County Register of Deeds charges. Source: Benzie County Register of Deeds page and MCL 600.2567.

The tax certificate comes from the County Treasurer and is required on warranty deeds, deeds containing a covenant of warranty, land contracts, assignments of land contracts, and master deeds for condominiums. Statute MCL 211.135 asks for proof that taxes were paid for the five years before the instrument.

sections.h2: Does Benzie County take eRecording, and does it cost extra?
sections.html:
Yes. The office lists four approved vendors: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. The vendor charges its own fee, and the Register of Deeds adds nothing on top for electronic filing.

If your deed needs a county tax certification, the office points filers to ePN, because it has a document router set up with that vendor. That saves a separate stop at the Treasurer's counter.

Searching the record is a separate matter. Land records and images reaching back to the mid 1800s are indexed by grantor and grantee. Public search through the Tapestry link is fee based, and a Laredo subscription is offered to title professionals. Call the office to arrange a subscription.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Benzie County deed?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds collects the Michigan state transfer tax at recording, and the county page links to the county act (MCL 207.505) and the state act (MCL 207.526). Statewide, the state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it, which is $7.50 per $1,000. Ask the office for the county portion that applies to your deed.

At the Census median owner occupied value for Benzie County of $285,700, the state tax alone would be $2,145, since $285,700 rounds up to 572 units of $500. That is a real cost to plan for in a lakeside sale.

Several transfers are exempt from the state tax under MCL 207.526, and the exemption must be written on the instrument.

  • Consideration under $100, security instruments, leases and mineral rights.
  • Conveyances from a person to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • Court judgments or orders that set no money price, and deeds that fix a boundary or correct a title flaw.
  • Land contracts where legal title has not yet passed, and transfers made in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What kinds of documents does the Benzie County office record?
sections.html:
The office describes its services as recording legal documents tied to land, and the list is long. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or an estate settlement.

  • Warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, mineral deeds, and administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, assignments of mortgage and discharges of mortgage.
  • State and federal tax liens, circuit court orders and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most on an older loan. After a mortgage is paid, the lender records a discharge, and the buyer's title company will look for it in this office before it clears title.

sections.h2: What steps should a Benzie County seller follow before recording?
sections.html:
Order of work saves time at a small county counter. Start with the title commitment so you know which liens must be discharged. Next, ask the Treasurer for the tax certificate if the deed carries a warranty, or send the deed through ePN so the certification is routed for you. Then confirm the full price on the deed, because transfer tax is computed on the stated consideration.

Finally, pick the delivery method. In person works during the 8:30 to 5:00 weekday window. Mail works if you include a stamped return envelope. eRecording works if your closing agent already uses one of the four vendors. If a document is for a family transfer, state the exemption on its face so the tax is not collected by mistake.

sections.h2: Which other Benzie County offices matter in a sale?
sections.html:
The Treasurer works from the upper level of the same Government Center, at 231-882-0011, with the same 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. hours. That office administers the delinquent tax process under Michigan's Public Act 206, holds the tax rolls, and takes delinquent tax online with a 2.49 percent convenience fee, minimum $1.50, or a $1.00 fee for an e-check.

The Equalization Department is on the lower level, Suite 130, at 231-882-0015. It handles parcel maps, parcel descriptions and values, property sales information, tax maps and millage rates, and it links to a parcel search and to FEMA flood map change forms, which matter near the shore.

The register also acts as chair of the county Plat Board for new subdivisions and as a U.S. passport acceptance agent.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Benzie County housing?
sections.html:
Benzie is small and growing. QuickFacts estimates 18,568 residents for July 2025, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 base, across 319.7 square miles of land. About 31.1 percent are 65 or older.

The county counts 12,682 housing units but only 7,708 households, and 87.8 percent of homes are owner occupied. Median value is $285,700 and median household income is $74,834 for 2020 to 2024. Building permits reached 136 in 2025. For a seller, the gap between units and households is worth a question to the title agent about whether the owner, a buyer or a prior owner lives elsewhere, since that affects who signs and where papers are mailed.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Benzie County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 per document, no matter the number of pages. Add $3.00 for each additional instrument a single document assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds charge for eRecording?
faqs.a: No. The office adds no fee, though the eRecording vendor you pick will charge its own. Approved vendors are Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a deed in Benzie County?
faqs.a: For warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds, yes. The certificate costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions, plus 20 cents for each extra description.

faqs.q: Can the Benzie County Register of Deeds draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot prepare blank documents or give legal advice, so use an attorney or a title company to draft and review the deed.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 231-882-0016 or visit Suite 202 of the Government Center at 448 Court Place in Beulah, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
